result.rationale: The migration inserts raw site_setting values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `https?://` and paths. Since `record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host`, a stored value like 'http://example.com' (which the old site setting examples/specs show existed, e.g. Fabricate(:embeddable_host, host: 'http://discourse.org')) would never match a referer host, breaking embedding post-upgrade. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` backfills rows using raw SQL string interpolation: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` comes directly from the old `site_settings` value split by newlines. This bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. As a result, previously-accepted entries like `http://discourse.org` (explicitly handled by the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` logic) would be stored verbatim in `embeddable_hosts.host`. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the referer URL and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, e.g. `eviltrout.com`, which will not match a stored value like `http://eviltrout.com`, causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` to raise `InvalidAccess`.
